 Pakistan host India in an International Friendly at Bangabandhu National Stadium on Thursday, 5 November 2026, with kick-off scheduled for 10:30. Even so, the previous five meetings between these sides all went India’s way, so the historical record offers a counterpoint to the current form.

 Pakistan performance check
 Pakistan’s recent form is the clearest positive in the build-up to this friendly. They have won three matches in a row, recording seven goals scored and none conceded. Their latest result was a 2–0 victory over Afghanistan, which also serves as their most recent International Friendly result in the supplied data. That clean-sheet win suggests a team with confidence and defensive organisation, while the wider three-game run shows they have been able to find the net consistently.
 The five-match picture is more mixed: Pakistan have three wins and two defeats, with no draws. That longer view tempers the impressive three-match streak, but their immediate momentum remains strong compared with India’s. No league standings are relevant for this International Friendly, and no coach’s name was supplied for Pakistan, so we cannot reliably identify the coach or make claims about the team’s position in a competition. Their recent results nonetheless give them a credible platform, particularly if they can maintain the defensive discipline shown against Afghanistan.
 India’s current form
 India come into the match after a difficult sequence. Across their last seven games, they have recorded no wins, two draws and five defeats, scoring four goals and conceding 18. Their most recent outing ended in a 6–1 loss to Uruguay, a result that will raise questions about defensive resilience ahead of this meeting. It is also listed as their latest International Friendly, so there is no more recent result in the supplied record to suggest that they have already turned the corner.
 India’s last five matches show two draws and three defeats, with no victories. That run contrasts sharply with Pakistan’s latest winning streak, although the historical rivalry provides India with a potential source of confidence. No standings or coach’s name were included in the match information, so India’s current ranking and the identity of their coach cannot be confirmed here. Their main challenge will be to tighten up at the back while finding a way to make their attacking chances count.
 The last direct duels
 The head-to-head record is emphatic: India have won all five of the last five meetings across all competitions, while Pakistan have no wins and there have been no draws. The latest listed encounter finished 4–0 to India, and the same 4–0 result is recorded for the most recent meeting in International Friendlies.
 That history makes India the dominant side in this rivalry over the sample provided, but it does not automatically settle the outlook for this match. Pakistan’s current three-win run and clean sheets are a substantial contrast to their recent head-to-head record. India will hope their past success carries over, while Pakistan have an opportunity to show that their present form can change the balance.
 Match conclusion and prediction
 Pakistan appear to have the stronger current momentum: they have won three straight games, scored seven goals and conceded none during that sequence. India’s recent results are far less convincing, especially after the 6–1 defeat to Uruguay. On form alone, Pakistan have reason to feel confident at Bangabandhu National Stadium.
 However, India’s record of five wins from the last five meetings cannot be ignored, and their 4–0 success in the latest listed encounter makes the historical case for the visitors clear. With no odds available and no confirmed betting tip supplied, choosing a side would be speculative. The most responsible conclusion is that Pakistan’s form gives them a chance to challenge the established head-to-head pattern, but there is not enough information to endorse a specific 1/X/2 or both-teams-to-score bet.
